chunks: And with this chain from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever leaves his house or the house of another and meets a chestnut horse with a white blaze, or one with a white spot on its forehead, that is the best of lives; he will encounter nothing on that day except joy. And if he set out for a need and met such a horse, Allah will fulfill his need.

key_terms.سَائِلٌ: Flowing (referring to the white spot extending down)
key_terms.غُرَّةٌ: A white spot on the forehead
key_terms.وَضَحٌ: A white blaze on the face

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of seeing a chestnut horse with a white blaze in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition of *al-ghayb* (divine signs), this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) highlights the spiritual significance of encountering a chestnut horse with a white blaze or a weeping forehead spot, viewing it as a potent omen of *al-'ish* (complete well-being). This specific physical characteristic of the horse is interpreted as a divine indicator that all worldly and spiritual needs will be fulfilled with joy on that day, reflecting the broader Islamic belief in finding blessings in natural phenomena.
